title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is Grothendieck's p. 690 (archive p. 674) in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes. It closes a section on the auxiliary groups attached to a group 𝔊^+ with distinguished generators ρ, σ. These generators are presumably modelled on the elliptic generators of orders 2 and 3 of (P)SL2(Ẑ) or its profinite analogues. The ambient objects are:
- Z_{ρ,σ}, the set of 'twisted' automorphisms u = (u, μ, ε2, ε3). These normalize L0 and send ρ, σ to conjugates of powers.
- A small quotient group γ_{ρ,σ} of signs/units.
- The groups Γ_{ρ,σ}, G_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ} and their 'natural' (♮) variants. The previous page relates them by fibre products over γ_{ρ,σ} and by isomorphisms GT̂^+/GT̂^♮ ≅ G/G^♮ ≅ M/M^♮.

The page title says G_{ρ,σ} and M_{ρ,σ} serve as 'environnements' (ambient catch-all groups) for the ♮-groups.

(89) Grothendieck fixes an element τ'_M in M^G_{ρ,σ} lying over an element τ'_γ ∈ γ_{ρ,σ}. Here τ is presumably the orientation-reversing / 'complex conjugation' type involution. He writes τ'_M as a triple (τ'_ρ, τ'_σ, τ'_G), with τ'_ρ ∈ N^G_ρ, τ'_σ ∈ N^G_σ and τ'_G ∈ G_{ρ,σ}. The N^G are normalizer-type groups of the generators. This matches the description of elements of M as compatible triples.

(90) This gives a commutative square. Its top row is 𝔖^G_τ ↪ M^G_{ρ,σ}, its bottom row is 𝔖 → M_{ρ,σ}, and the vertical maps are the natural ones.
- 𝔖^G is the inverse image in M_{ρ,σ} of the order-2 subgroup {1, τ'_γ} ⊂ γ_{ρ,σ}.
- 𝔖 is the inverse image in M_{ρ,σ} of {1, τ_γ}.
So 𝔖 and 𝔖^G are index-≤2 'real' or 'decomposition-like' subgroups singled out by an involution. Morally they are the analogue of the extension by Gal(ℂ/ℝ) of the geometric group, i.e. groups of the shape π1 ⋊ {1, complex conjugation}.

Grothendieck then notes that the 'diagrammes' of p. 584 (word uncertain) can be redone 'with G's attached'. He decides to try to avoid re-developing the links with Ξ_{ρ,σ}, SG_{ρ,σ} etc., keeping the option of returning to them later.

The next page begins §6 'Fonctorialités': functoriality under surjections 𝔊 → 𝔊'. The page is thus a bookkeeping transition. It records the involution-element and the index-2 subgroups it defines inside the ambient groups, then moves on.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is mostly notation-setting.
In (89) the third component's target was heavily overwritten. 'G_{ρ,σ}' is the most plausible reading, but uncertain.
It is not specified whether τ'_M is unique or only determined up to the kernel of M^G → γ; the page just says 'un élément'.

ideas.what: A distinguished involution-type element τ'_M in the ambient group M^G_{ρ,σ} lifting an element τ'_γ of the sign group, written as a triple of components in normalizers N^G_ρ, N^G_σ and in G_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: Lift of complex conjugation / orientation reversal into the (extended) GT-type automorphism group; the GT̂ action extended to include the image of complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT; Ihara, Lochak–Schneps and others for complex conjugation inside GT̂ and for real structures
ideas.where_published: Complex conjugation and Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on the Teichmüller tower are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Subgroups 𝔖, 𝔖^G of M_{ρ,σ} defined as inverse images of the order-2 subgroups {1,τ_γ}, {1,τ'_γ} of γ_{ρ,σ}, with the commutative square (90)
ideas.modern_name: Index-2 'real' subgroups / decomposition subgroups of an involution in an extension

ideas.what: Ambient 'catch-all' groups G_{ρ,σ}, M_{ρ,σ} in which the ♮-groups (the GT̂-related ones) sit as normal subgroups with quotients isomorphic to GT̂^+/GT̂^♮
ideas.modern_name: Extensions of GT̂-type groups by sign/orientation groups (GT̂ versus its full or orientation-extended versions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a transitional bookkeeping page. It sets up an involution element and the inverse images of order-2 subgroups in auxiliary groups, then defers the remaining links. Nothing here goes beyond routine group-theoretic setup within Grothendieck's own (unpublished) GT̂ formalism.
transcription_corrections: In (89) and in both legends of (90), the target group is lowercase γ_{ρ,σ}, not Γ_{ρ,σ}. Read 'τ'_γ ∈ γ_{ρ,σ}' and '{1,τ'_γ} ⊂ γ_{ρ,σ}', consistent with the fibre products over γ_{ρ,σ} on the previous page.
The legend for 𝔖^G reads 'im. inverse dans M_{ρ,σ} de {1,τ'_γ}', i.e. inverse image (preimage), not 'ens. pts invariants'. Likewise for 𝔖: 'im. inv. dans M_{ρ,σ} de {1,τ_γ}'.
The struck-out phrase in (89) is 'déduit de τ'_γ', replaced by 'au dessus de τ'_γ ∈ γ_{ρ,σ}'.
The last paragraph reads 'les liens avec Ξ_{ρ,σ}, SG_{ρ,σ}' (Xi, likely with an overbar), not Σ_{ρ,σ}. This is consistent with the next page mentioning Ξ^𝔊_{ρ,σ}.
The word before 'de p. 584' is illegible; 'bordiliques' is a doubtful reading.
